content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice, puffed is a whole‑grain rice that has been expanded through a high‑temperature puffing process. It retains the bran and germ of the grain, offering a light, crunchy texture similar to puffed rice. The product is commonly used in snack mixes, breakfast cereals, and as a topping for various dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Puffing is achieved by exposing the grain to high heat and pressure, creating a porous, airy structure.
Because it is whole‑grain, puffed brown rice contains more fiber and nutrients than puffed white rice.
It is a staple in many Asian desserts and light snack recipes.
Low moisture content gives it a long shelf life.
The product is gluten‑free, making it suitable for gluten‑free diets.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of magnesium and selenium
items.content: These minerals are important for muscle function, nerve health, and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains vitamin B1 (thiamine)
items.content: Thiamine aids in converting carbohydrates into energy.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Brown rice raises blood sugar more slowly than white rice.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to rice.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: Whole grains can contain trace amounts of arsenic; a varied diet helps minimize exposure.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Because it is light and airy, it can be eaten in large quantities, increasing overall calorie intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Puffed brown rice can be enjoyed as a snack on its own, added to muesli, yogurt, salads, soups, or used in baking. Lightly seasoning with salt or spices enhances its flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For extended storage, keep it in the refrigerator to prevent moisture absorption.
